When the screen turns off, aggressive OEM ROMs (Xiaomi, OPPO, OnePlus, Vivo) cut network for non-whitelisted apps. The bot will only deliver during occasional maintenance windows. Tap to whitelist Moxw.
Lets Moxw tap, swipe, scroll, read screen content, and take screenshots when the LLM uses the Screen automation tools.
Moxw needs accessibility permission to perform taps, swipes, and read the screen for the LLM. Open Settings → Accessibility → Installed Apps → Moxw and turn it on.
When system settings writes the switch back to off, re-assert the enabled entry directly with the Shizuku permission Moxw already holds - no trip through system settings.
Shizuku required: Moxw has not been granted the Shizuku permission yet.

Android 13 and later blocks this toggle for apps installed outside an app store. Open the app info page → ⋮ (top right) → Allow restricted settings, then come back and switch Moxw on. If that ⋮ entry is missing, tap the greyed switch once so the system offers it.
Getting revoked? Allow-list Moxw

Some systems (Xiaomi/Huawei/OPPO and others) reap background apps, and the accessibility service is dropped with them — the tools then fail with \"service not running\" even though the switch reads ON. Allow Moxw to autostart, allow it background battery use, and lock it in the recents list.

OriginOS power saving frequently drops the accessibility service, so the tools intermittently report \"service not running\". Do all three: 1) Settings → Apps & permissions → Permission manager → Moxw → Autostart; 2) Settings → Battery → Background power consumption → Moxw → Allow high background power; 3) in the recents screen, pull Moxw down (or tap its card) to lock it.

HyperOS power saving frequently drops the accessibility service, so the tools intermittently report \"service not running\". Do all three: 1) Settings → Apps → Moxw → Battery saver → No restrictions; 2) Settings → Apps → Moxw → Autostart; 3) in the recents screen, pull Moxw down (or tap its card) to lock it.

HarmonyOS power saving frequently drops the accessibility service, so the tools intermittently report \"service not running\". Do all three: 1) Settings → Apps → App launch → Moxw → turn off Auto-manage, then enable Autostart / Secondary launch / Run in background; 2) Settings → Battery → More battery settings → allow Moxw to keep running; 3) in the recents screen, pull Moxw down to lock it.

ColorOS power saving frequently drops the accessibility service, so the tools intermittently report \"service not running\". Do all three: 1) Settings → Apps → App management → Moxw → Battery usage → allow full background behaviour (+ allow autostart); 2) allow the app to start up automatically; 3) in the recents screen, tap the card menu → Lock.
Auto-discovered list of every permission Moxw uses, with a one-tap grant button for each.

On-device. Requires Pixel 8/9/10 with the AICore app installed AND enrollment in the GenAI Prompt-API early-access program (separate opt-in). If you see ErrorCode 606 / FEATURE_NOT_FOUND on first run, you have AICore installed but not the Prompt-API channel — request access via the GenAI Prompt-API early-access form, then reboot. Tool calling is supported via prompt engineering — Gemini Nano emits <tool_call> markup which Moxw parses and dispatches.
Moxw needs notification access to read incoming notifications. Open Settings → Notification access → Notification access and enable Moxw.

Workflows are enabled. Some trigger types need permissions the toggle can't request:

• Geofences (you arrive somewhere): Settings → Apps → Moxw → Permissions → Location → Allow all the time.
• Notification arrives: Settings → Apps → Special access → Notification access → enable Moxw.
• App launches/closes: Settings → Accessibility → enable Moxw.
• Bluetooth connect/disconnect: grant BLUETOOTH_CONNECT when the system asks.

Schedule, WiFi, headphones, power, screen on/off, and battery triggers work right out of the box. The assistant will flag any extra setup at the moment you author a workflow that needs it.

Install Shizuku from its GitHub releases page, then start its service: from the Shizuku app on a rooted device, or by pairing wireless debugging on Android 11+ (Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code, then run the start command Shizuku shows you). Once the service is running, tap Permission above to grant Moxw access.
